key_insight: IGA-KAN boosts isogeometric PDE solves by fitting local closed-form Kolmogorov-Arnold ridge models to the IGA solution and PDE residuals, then blending them only where they help.
engineering_relevance: It offers a mesh-based, error-controlled way to improve forward and inverse PDE accuracy without neural-network training instability or extra Galerkin unknowns.
method: Run a standard IGA Galerkin solve to obtain baseline u_h on exact NURBS geometry.
On each knot-vertex patch, fit a closed-form local KAN ridge model to the strong-form PDE, boundary data, and u_h using one batched linear least-squares solve.
Blend local corrections with IGA hat functions and use an a posteriori safeguard to keep the original IGA solution where the local model is not reliable.
evidence_signal: Across eight benchmark PDEs, the method reduced IGA errors by factors of 4.2–90 in L^2 and 4.1–220 in H^1, and in one inverse problem it recovered an unknown source 167× more accurately than IGA.
watch_item: Performance depends on patchwise model fitting and the a posteriori selection rule, so robustness may vary if the local least-squares system is ill-conditioned or the safeguard is too conservative.
paper_title: IGA-KAN: Isogeometric Analysis with Physics-Informed Closed-Form Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for Forward and Inverse PDEs
